# Signed cylinder propagation and marked polygons on the honeycomb lattice

Coordinate `EN-115-000-0003-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M2-B-ML-M-0478` | `PM-237.5` | status ACTIVE | original slug `Signed-cylinder-propagation-and-marked-polygons-on-the-honeycomb-lattice-September-26-2026` | date 2026-09-26 | derived from the openai/math preprint Signed-cylinder-propagation-and-marked-polygons-on-the-honeycomb-lattice-September-26-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "At the critical activity and loop fugacity two, we prove a 1/6 partition exponent for disjoint honeycomb polygons separating opposite marks on a balanced infinite cylinder, and a 1/12 planar nesting exponent. For ordered first-exit chords in a regular hexagon of side <i>R</i>, with both boundary ports summed and diameter at least $`R/10`$, the finite critical partition is $`R^{3/4+o(1)}`$ and the normalized mean length is $`R^{4/3+o(1)}`$. A separate two-bond estimate on tilted cylinders with controlled site proportions bounds the length-square mass of planar polygons of diameter at most <i>H</i>, modulo translations, by $`H^{2/3+o(1)}`$.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> At the critical activity and loop fugacity two, we prove a 1/6 partition exponent for disjoint honeycomb polygons separating opposite marks on a balanced infinite cylinder, and a 1/12 planar nesting exponent. For ordered first-exit chords in a regular hexagon of side <i>R</i>, with both boundary ports summed and diameter at least $`R/10`$, the finite critical partition is $`R^{3/4+o(1)}`$ and the normalized mean length is $`R^{4/3+o(1)}`$. A separate two-bond estimate on tilted cylinders with controlled site proportions bounds the length-square mass of planar polygons of diameter at most <i>H</i>, modulo translations, by $`H^{2/3+o(1)}`$.

- **claim-cylinder-pressure-and-nesting** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-cylinder)): As $m\to\infty$ through even integers, $$G_m(2)=m^{1/6+o(1)},\qquad -\left.\frac{d^2}{dg^2}\log G_m(g)\right\|_{g=0}=O(\log m).$$ The derivative is the total basic weight of ordered incompatible pairs of separating cycles, including a cycle paired with itself. Locally uniformly for complex $\Theta$ with $\|\Re\Theta\|<\pi$, $$\|G_m(2\cos\Theta)\| \le m^{\Re(1/6-2\Theta^2/(3\pi^2))+o(1)}.$$ The planar partition satisfies $\mathcal Z(R)=R^{1/12+o(1)}$ as $R$ tends to infinity through integers.
  - Explanation: Establishes the balanced cylinder partition exponent, controls ordered incompatible separating cycles, and determines the planar nesting exponent.
- **claim-finite-chords-and-polygon-moment** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-hexagon)): For the chord law just defined, $$Z_R^{\rm chord}=R^{3/4+o(1)},\qquad \mathbb E_R^{\rm chord}N=R^{4/3+o(1)}.$$ Uniformly for honeycomb vertices $v$ at distance at most $R/10$ from the hexagon center, $$\mathbb P_R^{\rm chord}(v\in\gamma)=R^{-2/3+o(1)}.$$ Furthermore, for planar polygons modulo lattice translations, $$\label{j:polygon-square} \sum_{\operatorname{diam}\lambda\le H} x^{\|\lambda\|}\|\lambda\|^2\le H^{2/3+o(1)}.$$
  - Explanation: Determines the normalization, mean length, and bulk visit exponent for the specified chord ensemble, and bounds the translation-class polygon length-square mass.
- **claim-meromorphic-exchange-and-fusion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-local-exchange-fusion)): The entries of $R(\psi)$ are meromorphic, with possible poles at $\Delta_R(\psi)=0$. The following are identities of meromorphic matrix functions: $$\begin{split} R_{12}(t)R_{13}(t+\phi)R_{23}(\phi) &=R_{23}(\phi)R_{13}(t+\phi)R_{12}(t),\\ R_{12}(\phi)R_{21}(-\phi)&=I. \end{split}$$ In particular the second equality is a pointwise inverse identity where both factors are regular, and $R_{12}(0)=P_{12}$.* *For $\delta=2,3$, let $E_2=V$, $E_3=\mathbb C$, and define injective maps $J_\delta:E_\delta\to V\otimes V$ by $$\begin{aligned} J_2\|0\rangle&=\|00\rangle+x\sum_{k=\pm1}\lambda^k\|k,-k\rangle, &J_2\|k\rangle&=x(\|k,0\rangle+\|0,k\rangle)\quad(k=\pm1),\\ J_3(1)&=\sum_{k=0,\pm1}\lambda^k\|k,-k\rangle. \end{aligned}$$ On $E_2$ let $s_{\rm f}\|k\rangle=k\|k\rangle$, and on $E_3$ let $s_{\rm f}=0$. Then $R_{12}(\delta\alpha)=J_\delta J_\delta^*$ and, writing $J=J_\delta$, $$R_{23}(\phi)R_{13}(\phi+\delta\alpha)(J\otimes I) =(J\otimes I)R_{\rm f}(\phi),\qquad R_{\rm f}(\phi)= \begin{cases} R(\phi+\alpha),&\delta=2,\\ I,&\delta=3. \end{cases}$$ The intertwining equality is again meromorphic in $\phi$.
  - Explanation: Supplies meromorphic exchange and inversion identities together with the local fusion embeddings and their transported actions.
- **claim-fusion-restriction-and-quotient** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-local-restriction)): Fix $\delta\in\{2,3\}$, put $W_\delta=\operatorname{im}J_\delta \subset V_1\otimes V_2$, and for another factor $V_k$ set $$F_{\delta,k}(\psi)=R_{2k}(\psi)R_{1k}(\psi+\delta\alpha).$$ At regular parameters the subspace $W_\delta\otimes V_k$ is invariant, and transporting the restriction through $J_\delta\otimes I$ gives $R_{\rm f}(\psi)$ from Lemma <a href="#j:local-exchange-fusion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="j:local-exchange-fusion">3</a>. At $\psi=0$ the full image of $F_{\delta,k}(0)$ lies in this subspace. Hence the induced operator on $\bigl((V_1\otimes V_2)/W_\delta\bigr)\otimes V_k$ is zero there and, near $z=e^{2i\psi}=1$, is holomorphic and divisible by $z-1$.* *The twist restricts by $p^{s_1+s_2}J_2=J_2p^{s_{\rm f}}$ and $p^{s_1+s_2}J_3=J_3$ for every $p\ne0$. There is also the meromorphic site intertwining $$\label{j:site-fusion} R_{a1}(\psi)R_{a2}(\psi+\delta\alpha)(I_a\otimes J_\delta) =(I_a\otimes J_\delta) \begin{cases} R_{a{\rm f}}(\psi+\alpha),&\delta=2,\\ I_a,&\delta=3. \end{cases}$$
  - Explanation: Identifies the invariant fused subspace and proves that the quotient action vanishes at the matching site, with a holomorphic divisibility statement.
- **claim-scalar-fourier-transform** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-fourier-kernel)): For $0<\beta<\pi$ and $\|\Im y\|<\pi-\beta$, $$\int_{\mathbb R}e^{iky}\frac{\sinh(\beta k)}{\sinh(\pi k)}\,dk =\frac{\sin\beta}{\cosh y+\cos\beta}.$$ The integral and its parameter derivatives converge locally uniformly on the indicated strip.
  - Explanation: Evaluates the scalar Fourier integral on its analytic strip and permits local parameter differentiation.
- **claim-normalizer-polynomials-and-reductions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-scalar-normalizers)): For every list size $M$, the functions $N_l$ are symmetric homogeneous polynomials of individual degree at most $l(M-1)$ for $M\ge1$, and $$\mathcal J=N N_2^*.$$ For $l=1,2$ and $X=(u,Z)$ of size $M\ge1$, their deletion values are $$\label{j:normalizer-deletion} N_l(0,Z)=\left(\prod_{z\in Z}z^l\right)N_l(Z), \qquad [u^{l(M-1)}]N_l(u,Z)=N_l(Z).$$ For $\delta=2,3$ all three satisfy $$\label{j:normalizer-fusion} N_l(u,q^\delta u,Z)=N_l(u,q^\delta u)\ \prod_{z\in Z}\ell_\delta(u,z)^l\ N_l(X_{\rm red}),\qquad X_{\rm red}=\begin{cases}(qu,Z)&\delta=2,\\Z&\delta=3.\end{cases}$$ At two sites, $$N(u,v)=u+v,\qquad N_2^*(u,v)=u^2+2(1+\sqrt2)uv+v^2.$$ Finally, $N$ and $N_2^*$ are nonzero at every homogeneous list $(b,\ldots,b)$ with $b\ne0$.
  - Explanation: Establishes polynomiality, degree bounds, factorization, deletion and fusion evaluations, and homogeneous nonvanishing of the scalar normalizers.
- **claim-separated-scale-transfer-blocks** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-separated-scales)): Let positive scales $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_r$ satisfy $\rho_{k+1}/\rho_k\to\infty$, and suppose $x_i/\rho_{k_i}$ tends to a finite nonzero limit. Choose consistent local square roots. Probe with $w/\rho_j$ tending to a finite nonzero limit for which the active local matrices are regular. The limiting row matrices are triangular in the grading $\sum_i k_i s_i$, with row grade at least column grade. Their diagonal grade blocks preserve every scale total $S_k=\sum_{i:k_i=k}s_i$ and act on the active scale $j$ with effective twist $$p_j=p q^{3\sum_{k\ne j}\operatorname{sgn}(j-k) S_k} .$$ Each block entry is the corresponding active-transfer entry multiplied by $F(s^{\rm row})/F(s^{\rm col})$, using the same diagonal matrix for every probe and twist, where $$F(s)=q^{(3/2)\sum_{l<i}\operatorname{sgn}(k_l-k_i)s_l s_i} ,$$ restricted to the block in question.
  - Explanation: Shows that separated site magnitudes produce triangular limiting transfers with conserved scale charges, effective twists, and a common diagonal similarity.
- **claim-selected-vacuum-polynomial-components** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-selected-vacuum-vectors)): Let $M\ge1$, let $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_M)$ be generic and nonzero, and choose $t_j$ with $t_j^2=x_j$. For $\sigma\in\{-1,0,1\}^M$ with $\sum_j\sigma_j=0$, define from the vacuum-normalized vectors $R_i=\Pi_i\|0\rangle$ and $L_{-i}=\langle0\|\Pi_{-i}$ the functions $$V_\sigma^R(X)= \frac{N(X)(R_i)_\sigma}{\prod_jt_j^{\sigma_j^2}}, \qquad V_\sigma^L(X)= \frac{N(X)(L_{-i})_\sigma}{\prod_jt_j^{\sigma_j^2}}.$$ They are independent of the choices of square-root signs and extend to polynomials in $\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_M]$ satisfying $$\deg_{x_j}V_\sigma^\epsilon\le M-1-\sigma_j^2 \qquad(\epsilon=R,L).$$ Write $X_{\widehat j}$ and $\widehat\sigma$ for deletion of coordinate $j$, and set $V_\varnothing^R=V_\varnothing^L=1$. If $\sigma_j=0$, then for either superscript $$\left.V_\sigma(X)\right\|_{x_j=0} =\left(\prod_{k\ne j}x_k\right)V_{\widehat\sigma}(X_{\widehat j}), \qquad [x_j^{M-1}]V_\sigma(X)=V_{\widehat\sigma}(X_{\widehat j}).$$
  - Explanation: Clearing the selected vacuum components by the scalar normalizer and their parity factors yields ordinary polynomials with coordinate degree and deletion rules.
- **claim-cleared-scalar-vacuum-polynomial** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-scalar-vacuum-polynomial)): For two consecutive lists $A,B$, allowing either to be empty, and $h\ne0$, put $\mathscr G(X;A,B)=L_-D_A R_+$. Then $$\begin{split} N(X)^2\mathscr G(X;A,B) =\sum_{\substack{\sigma\in\{-1,0,1\}^M\\ \sum_j\sigma_j=0}} (ih)^{\sum_{j\in A}\sigma_j} \left(\prod_jx_j^{\sigma_j^2}\right) V_\sigma^L(X)V_\sigma^R(X). \end{split}$$ The empty-list value is 1. For $M\ge1$ it is a polynomial in $X$ with Laurent polynomial coefficients in $h$, of individual degree at most $2(M-1)$. For a deleted site $j$, its value at $x_j=0$ is the reduced polynomial times $\prod_{k\ne j}x_k^2$, and its coefficient of $x_j^{2(M-1)}$ is the reduced polynomial. Moreover $\mathscr G$ itself tends to the reduced $\mathscr G$ as $x_j\to0,\infty$ with generic spectators.
  - Explanation: Expanding the diagonal insertion in selected vacuum components gives a polynomial scalar observable, including empty-list, deletion, and endpoint limits.
- **claim-unique-scalar-characterization** (classification, [source](#stmt-j-scalar-characterization)): The family $\mathscr F_{A,B}$ is the unique family in $\mathbb C(h)[X]$ with the following properties. The empty-list value is 1. For $M=\|A\|+\|B\|\ge1$, each polynomial is symmetric within the two groups and has individual degree at most $2(M-1)$. Deleting a site $j$ gives $$\left.\mathscr F_{A,B}\right\|_{x_j=0} =\left(\prod_{k\ne j}x_k^2\right)\mathscr F_{\widehat j}, \qquad [x_j^{2(M-1)}]\mathscr F_{A,B}=\mathscr F_{\widehat j}.$$ For two sites $u,q^\delta u$ in one group, $\delta=2,3$, it satisfies $$\mathscr F_{A,B}(u,q^\delta u,Z) =(u+q^\delta u)^2 \left(\prod_{z\in Z}\ell_\delta(u,z)^2\right) \mathscr F_{\rm red}(X_{\rm red}),$$ with $X_{\rm red}$ as in <a href="#j:normalizer-fusion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="j:normalizer-fusion">[j:normalizer-fusion]</a>. When $\|A\|=\|B\|$, its quotient by $N^2$ has the paired-scale limit <a href="#j:paired-vacuum-limit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="j:paired-vacuum-limit">[j:paired-vacuum-limit]</a> at generic fixed pair ratios.
  - Explanation: Characterizes the scalar polynomial family uniquely by its group symmetries, degree bounds, deletion values, fusion values, and balanced paired-scale normalization.
- **claim-exact-finite-spin-sum** (construction, [source](#stmt-j-finite-spin-formula)): For $h\ne0$ and the two-list vacuum observable at generic sites, $$\label{j:finite-spin-sum} \begin{aligned} N(X)^2\mathscr G ={}&\sum_{\substack{(s_i)\\ \sum_{i\in A}s_i=\sum_{i\in B}s_i=Q}} h^Q \prod_i (d_{\sigma(i)}x_i)^{s_i^2}\\ &\qquad\cdot\prod_{\text{same-group pairs }i,j}p_{s_i s_j}(x_i,x_j) \prod_{\text{cross pairs }i,j}p'_{s_i s_j}(x_i,x_j), \end{aligned}$$ where $\sigma(i)={\rm a},{\rm b}$ indicates group and $Q$ ranges freely subject to the displayed equality. These auxiliary spins in group $B$ use the equal-sum convention. The combined expression is evaluated at same-group coincidences by its polynomial limit.
  - Explanation: Expresses the cleared observable as an explicit finite spin sum with equal group charges; coincident same-group sites require the combined polynomial limit.
- **claim-regulated-pfaffian-and-fixed-site-limit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-c7-regulated-pfaffian)): For every fixed $T>0$, $m\in\mathbb N_0$, and $\theta\in\mathbb C$, on the full-probability event of analytic samples described above, the Wick expansion in <a href="#c7:contour-current" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c7:contour-current">[c7:contour-current]</a> terminates after order $m$ in each species. Its value is independent of the admissible circle enclosing $W$, and its contour coefficients extend holomorphically to the coalescing lists $\|w_l\|<r/4$. The average <a href="#c7:regulated-contour" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c7:regulated-contour">[c7:regulated-contour]</a> is holomorphic there and its denominator is nonzero. In particular $\mathfrak C_{0,T}=1$.* *For fixed $m\ge1$ and $\theta\in\mathbb C$, $$\label{c7:regulated-limit} \lim_{T\longrightarrow\infty}\mathfrak C_{m,T} =\frac{N(1,\ldots,1)^2}{P_0}\, G_{A,B}(h+h^{-1}),\qquad \|A\|=\|B\|=m.$$ This limit is locally uniform in $\theta$.
  - Explanation: Proves finite Wick termination and holomorphic confluence at fixed period, then recovers the physical observable by sending the period to infinity at fixed site count.
- **claim-conditional-angular-trace** (theorem, [source](#stmt-c7-angular-trace)): Fix $T>0$, $m\in\mathbb N_0$, $\theta\in\mathbb C$, and a homogeneous analytic sample as above. The normalizing trace is $$Z_\Gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}\Gamma =\prod_{r\in\frac12+\mathbb N_0}(1-\mathbf q^{6r})>0.$$ For $s\ge1$, if the folded coordinates have strictly increasing imaginary parts with total range less than $1$, then $$\label{c7:angular-wick} \left(-\frac{2\pi i}{a_*T}\right)^s \frac{\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\Gamma\Psi_{j_1}(v_1)\cdots \Psi_{j_{2s}}(v_{2s})\bigr)}{Z_\Gamma} = \operatorname{Pf}_{1\le a,b\le2s} C^{[T]}\bigl(v_b-v_a+i(j_b-j_a)\bigr).$$ The trace in this display denotes its absolutely convergent ordered mode sum. For $s=0$ both sides are $1$. The formula at other nonsingular coordinates is its meromorphic continuation; odd products vanish.* *Let $P_N$ project onto the energy-$N$ subspace, for $N\in\frac12\mathbb N_0$. For a fixed finite word $Y$ of exponentials of the currents $X_{bc}(f)$, with periodic coefficients analytic on a common strip of positive width, there are $C,c>0$ such that $$\label{c7:graded-current-bound} \\|P_{N'}YP_N\\|\le C e^{C\sqrt{N+1}}e^{-c\|N'-N\|}.$$ The constants can be taken locally uniform in numerical parameters multiplying the currents in the exponentials. In particular the energy-level trace with $\Gamma$ is absolutely convergent, as are its exponential series of scalar trace coefficients.* *For the homogeneous contour expression <a href="#c7:contour-current" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c7:contour-current">[c7:contour-current]</a> and the fixed analytic sample, $$\label{c7:four-current-trace} \mathcal C_\sigma =\frac1{Z_\Gamma}\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm gr}\!\left( \Gamma e^{X_{23}(b_+^{-1})}e^{X_{21}(b)} e^{-X_{12}(b^{-1})}e^{-X_{16}(b_-)}\right).$$ Here the absolutely convergent trace furnished by <a href="#c7:graded-current-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c7:graded-current-bound">[c7:graded-current-bound]</a> is $$\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm gr}(\Gamma Y) =\sum_N\mathbf q^N \operatorname{tr}_{P_N\mathcal F}(\mathcal U P_NYP_N),$$ where $\mathcal F$ is the fermionic exterior space. The convergence assertions concern this fixed sample.
  - Explanation: Realizes the conditional Wick contractions as a normalized fermionic trace and controls the graded current series for each fixed analytic sample.
- **claim-exact-horizontal-gas** (theorem, [source](#stmt-c7-gas-identity)): Fix $d_-<0<d$ in the respective nonzero displacement ranges of Theorem <a href="#j:absolute-stability" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="j:absolute-stability">15</a>, with $0<\|d_-\|<d<1/2$. Fix also a compact set $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$ of values of $\theta$. There is an integer $T_0$, independent of $m$, such that for every integer $T\ge T_0$ and every finite integer $m\ge0$, the gas <a href="#c7:gas-definition" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c7:gas-definition">[c7:gas-definition]</a> converges absolutely, uniformly for $\theta\in\Omega$ at that $m,T$, and satisfies $$\label{c7:regulator-gas} \mathfrak C_{m,T}=c(T)e^{m^2\kappa_T}Z_{m,T},\qquad c(T)=\frac{\sqrt{8/9}}{8\sqrt{2T}\,D_\ell} \left(\frac{\sqrt T D_W}{Z_\Gamma}\right)^2D_g, \qquad D_\ell=\sum_{j\in8\mathbb Z}e^{-4\pi j^2/T}.$$ In particular it holds along $T=bn$ for any fixed integer block length $b\ge T_0$ and every positive integer $n$. This common period domain allows $T$ to remain fixed while $m$ varies through finite integers. The absolute bounds may depend on $m,T$ and the fixed displacements; no bound uniform in $m$ or limiting assertion as $d_-\uparrow0$ or $d\downarrow0$ is made.
  - Explanation: Identifies the absolutely convergent horizontal gas with the regulator on a common integer-period domain independent of the finite site count.
- **claim-absolute-gas-stability** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-absolute-stability)): There is $0<d_0<1/2$ with the following property. Fix a compact set $\Theta\subset\mathbb C$, and fix either a pre-collision displacement $-d_0<d<0$ or a post-collision displacement $0<d<d_0$. There are constants $c>0$ and $C<\infty$, depending on $d$ and $\Theta$, such that the following holds for every positive integer $T$ and $\theta\in\Theta$.* *Consider a finite configuration $\mathcal Y$ with distinct real positions on $\mathbb R/T\mathbb Z$, using the six basic labels in the pre-collision case and those labels together with $F_{\rm pair}$ in the post-collision case. Give it a state path $p$ with jumps $-q_i$ and closure in $\mathbb Z^2/8\mathbb Z(1,-1)$. Let $n_j$ be the number of physical particles in $[j,j+1)$, and let $$p_{c,j}=\frac{p_1(j+)+p_2(j+)}{\sqrt2}, \qquad 0\le j<T.$$ Then $$\left\|W_{d,\theta}(\mathcal Y,p)\right\| \ \le\ \exp\!\left(CT-c\sum_{j=0}^{T-1}(n_j^2+p_{c,j}^2)\right)$$ in the post-collision case. The same bound holds for $W^{\rm pre}_{d,\Re\theta}(\mathcal Y,p)$ in the pre-collision case.
  - Explanation: Bounds absolute configuration weights by quadratic confinement of physical particle counts and common charges, separately before and after collision at fixed nonzero displacement.
- **claim-coercive-height-matrix** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-stability-coercivity)): For each fixed displacement in Theorem <a href="#j:absolute-stability" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="j:absolute-stability">15</a>, the physical matrix $\mathcal H'(k)$ has nullspace $\mathcal N$ for every $k>0$. On the quotient by $\mathcal N$, it is bounded below near zero by a positive constant times $$kI+\frac{\boldsymbol c\boldsymbol c^t}{k},$$ and it converges exponentially at infinity to a strictly positive matrix $\mathcal H'(\infty)$. The physical limit $Q_\infty=\mathcal H(\infty)$ is entrywise nonnegative.* *Consequently one can choose $0<e<2$ and $\gamma>0$, depending on the fixed displacement, such that $$\label{j:stability-J} J(k):=\mathcal H'(k)-\mathcal H'(\infty)\tanh(ek), \qquad \frac{J(k)}{k}\ge \gamma e^{-k^2}\left( \mathfrak n\mathfrak n^t+ \frac{\boldsymbol c\boldsymbol c^t}{k^2}\right),\quad k>0,$$ where $\mathfrak n$ is the all-ones vector on the actual physical labels. In the pre-collision case the matrices in this statement are restricted to the six basic labels.
  - Explanation: Controls the physical height matrix on its fixed nullspace quotient and isolates a positive Fourier component that detects particle count and common charge.
- **claim-block-kernel-trace-realization** (construction, [source](#stmt-j-block-kernel)): Use the state space, measure, and successor rule <a href="#j:successor-state" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="j:successor-state">[j:successor-state]</a>. Suppose the local kernel satisfies <a href="#j:local-gauge" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="j:local-gauge">[j:local-gauge]</a>, and use the tail data and edge operator <a href="#j:tail-data" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="j:tail-data">[j:tail-data]</a>–<a href="#j:bargmann-edge" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="j:bargmann-edge">[j:bargmann-edge]</a> with the bounds just proved. On $L^2$ of states with these Bargmann fibers, give an allowed edge the operator-valued kernel $$\label{j:gauged-kernel} e^{\Phi(S')-\Phi(S)}w_\theta(S,S')\,\mu(Y)\,\mathcal K(S,S'),$$ and give every other edge value zero. The choices of $\mu(Y)$ used in this section are one, the indicator that every label is $M$ or $F_{\rm pair}$, and the products of the specified balanced periodized or infinite-volume $B$ factors. Their per-particle factors have modulus at most one. For sufficiently large fixed $b$, these kernels are Hilbert–Schmidt uniformly in those choices and in $\theta\in D$. The same conclusion permits fixed polynomial factors in the particle counts. For the fixed gauge on $D$, the kernels form holomorphic families in Hilbert–Schmidt norm on the open parameter neighborhood $\mathcal U_\theta$, with bounds uniform on compact subsets.* *For a product of $n\ge2$ such kernels, its trace is the absolutely convergent integral over closed successor sequences, with the gauge factors canceled and the Bargmann trace given by <a href="#j:bargmann-cycle" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="j:bargmann-cycle">[j:bargmann-cycle]</a>. In particular, let $T_j$ carry the specified periodized $B_T$ site factors for block $j$. Then, in increasing block order, $$\label{j:operator-gas-trace} \operatorname{tr}\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}T_j =\det(I-A_0^n)^{-1}Z_{m,bn}.$$
  - Explanation: Builds Hilbert–Schmidt propagation kernels whose closed-product traces recover the gas, with an auxiliary Bargmann factor carrying the interaction tail exactly.
- **claim-signed-trace-coefficient-extraction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-trace-extraction)): Let $E$ be a Hilbert–Schmidt operator on a complex Hilbert space with spectral radius one. Let $\mathcal P=\{\zeta\in\sigma(E):\|\zeta\|=1\}$. For each $\zeta\in\mathcal P$ let $P_\zeta$ be its Riesz projection, $d_\zeta=\operatorname{rank}P_\zeta$, and $J_\zeta=(E-\zeta I)P_\zeta$, with $J_\zeta^{q_\zeta}=0$ on $\operatorname{ran}P_\zeta$. Let $C$ be trace class. Suppose two countable families of bounded operators $W_+,W_-$ have integer lengths $\ell(W_\pm)\ge0$ and, for some $\epsilon>0$, $$\label{j:word-moment} \sum_{W_\pm}e^{\epsilon\ell(W_\pm)}\\|W_\pm\\|<\infty.$$ For integers $s\ge0$ put $$F_s=\sum_{\ell(W_+)+\ell(W_-)\le s} \operatorname{tr}(CW_+E^{s-\ell(W_+)-\ell(W_-)}W_-).$$ Assume that $a\ge0$ is an integer and $R\in\mathbb C$ satisfy $F_s-R\operatorname{tr}E^{s+a}\to0$ as $s\to\infty$. Only sufficiently large $s$, with $s+a\ge2$, are used in this limit. Then the coefficientwise absolutely convergent polynomial $$\mathcal P_\zeta(z)=\sum_{W_+,W_-}\zeta^{-\ell} \operatorname{tr}\left(CW_+ \left[\sum_{t=0}^{q_\zeta-1} \binom{z-\ell}{t}\zeta^{-t}J_\zeta^tP_\zeta\right]W_-\right), \quad \ell=\ell(W_+)+\ell(W_-),$$ is identically $R d_\zeta\zeta^a$. In particular, $$R=\frac{\mathcal P_\zeta(0)}{d_\zeta\zeta^a},\qquad \|R\|\le K\\|C\\|_1,$$ where $K$ depends on $E$ and the bounds in <a href="#j:word-moment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="j:word-moment">[j:word-moment]</a>, but not on $C$ or $a$. More precisely it may be chosen in terms of $\epsilon$, the two weighted word sums, the finite nilpotent orders $q_\zeta$, and the norms $\\|J_\zeta^tP_\zeta\\|$. Thus the conclusion is uniform for a family with uniform bounds on these data. No peripheral semisimplicity is assumed.
  - Explanation: Extracts peripheral exponential-polynomial coefficients from a vanishing difference of traces and bounds the physical scalar while retaining all nilpotent terms.
- **claim-even-polynomial-logarithmic-statistic** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-even-log-statistic)): Let $\mu(u)=2u/\sinh(\pi u)$, with its continuous value at zero, and let $P_m$ project in $L^2(\mu(u)\,du)$ onto the even polynomials of degree at most $2m-2$. If $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and even and satisfies $\|f(u)\|\le C e^{-c\|u\|}$ for some $C,c>0$, then $$\log\det(P_m e^fP_m\|_{\operatorname{ran}P_m}) =\frac{\log m}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}f(u)\,du+o(\log m).$$
  - Explanation: Determines the logarithmic determinant asymptotic for even continuous exponentially decaying multiplication tests compressed to the even-polynomial subspace.
- **claim-boundary-arch-mass** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-boundary)): Fix a port on a horizontal tessellation half-plane boundary. Let $W_R$ be the total critical weight $x^N$ of first-exit same-boundary arches reaching Euclidean distance at least $R$ from that port. Then $W_R=R^{-1/4+o(1)}$. If $H(d)$ is the mass of arches ending $d$ boundary steps to the right, then $$2\sin(\pi/8)\sum_{d>0}H(d)=1,\qquad \sum_{d\ge n}H(d)\le n^{-1/4+o(1)}.$$ The constants are unchanged by lattice translations and rotations.
  - Explanation: Determines the half-plane arch radius exponent, saturates the boundary balance, and bounds the endpoint tail.
- **claim-pinned-orbital-density** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-orbital-pin)): Let $\rho(0)$ be the one-point intensity at zero of <a href="#j:boundary-orbital-law" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="j:boundary-orbital-law">[j:boundary-orbital-law]</a>. Pinning one point there leaves $N=M-1$ positive points with density proportional to $$\Delta(k^2)^2\prod_{j=1}^N k_j^4w_0(k_j)\,I(k_1,\ldots,k_N,0).$$ The orbital integral here still uses the $2M$-dimensional orbit, with one zero pair in $D_k$. For its expectation $\mathbb E_{\rm pin}$, $$\begin{aligned} \frac{\sin\alpha}{\alpha}\frac{\rho(0)}{w_0(0)} \mathbb E_{\rm pin}\prod_{j=1}^N(1+k_j^{-2}) &\le -iK(i)\\ &\le\frac{\rho(0)}{w_0(0)} \mathbb E_{\rm pin}\prod_{j=1}^N(1+k_j^{-2}). \end{aligned}$$ Empty products have value one.
  - Explanation: Relates the boundary adjugate evaluation to a positive pinned orbital expectation and preserves the original orbit dimension after pinning.
- **claim-orbital-logarithmic-derivative** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-orbital-ward)): For either orbital factor, there are numbers $q_j$ such that $$\partial_{k_j}\log I^{(e)}=2q_j,\qquad 0\le q_j\le \min\left\{\alpha,\alpha^2k_j, \frac{\alpha^2}{\sum_{\ell=1}^N(k_j+k_\ell)^{-1}}\right\}.$$ The bounds are uniform in $N$.
  - Explanation: Bounds orbital logarithmic derivatives using positivity, the orbit norm, and reciprocal sums over the moving points.
- **claim-gamma-stochastic-comparisons** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-boundary-gamma-comparison)): For every fixed $b_+>6\alpha$, there is $\ell_+>0$ such that, with $\beta_+=b_+/\pi$, for all $N$ and $e=0,4$, $$\mathbb P_N[k^e W_{\ell_+,\beta_+}] \preceq_{\rm st}\mathbb O_N^{(e)}.$$ For fixed $0<b_-<6\alpha$ and $0<\epsilon<1$, there is $\ell_->0$ such that, with $\beta_-=b_-/\pi$ and for sufficiently large $N$, $$\mathcal L_{\mathbb O_N^{(e)}}(k_{\le m}\mid E,k_{>m}) \preceq_{\rm st}\mathbb P_m[k^eW_{\ell_-,\beta_-}]$$ for almost every later configuration compatible with $E$, where $m=\lfloor N^{1-\epsilon}\rfloor$.
  - Explanation: Sandwiches the orbital laws in the stochastic directions needed for decreasing pinned statistics, with a conditional comparison for the initial points.
- **claim-extremal-segment-mass** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-extremal-segment)): Fix a honeycomb vertex and two distinct height levels, with the fixed vertex on one level. The total critical weight of SAW segments from that vertex to any vertex on the other level, whose endpoints are opposite height extrema of the segment, is bounded by an absolute constant independent of the levels.
  - Explanation: Bounds endpoint-summed critical mass for segments whose endpoints are opposite height extrema, independently of their height separation.
- **claim-convex-cap-boundary-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-convex-cap)): Let $K\subset D$ be finite convex tessellation polygons sharing a starting port with the same inward direction. Let $L$ be the raw weight of first-exit chords of $D$ other than those confined to $K$ and ending at a boundary port shared by $K$ and $D$. Let $E$ be the raw weight of first-exit chords of $K$ ending on ports newly created by the restriction. Then $$\sin\alpha\,L\le E\le L/\sin\alpha.$$ The same conclusion holds with $D$ the saturated tessellation half-plane and $K$ a finite convex cap.
  - Explanation: Compares the lost chord mass under a convex restriction with the artificial exit mass, including the saturated half-plane case.
- **claim-interior-visit-and-nesting-identities** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-visit)): Let $D$ be a finite convex tessellation polygon and let $v$ be a honeycomb vertex not adjacent to a boundary port. Sum over all ordered first-exit boundary chords of $D$ that visit $v$, and put $$S_D(v)=\sum_{\gamma\ni v}x^{N(\gamma)}\cos(3T(\gamma)/8).$$ Let $Z_v$ be the partition of disjoint unoriented cycles in $D$ strictly enclosing $v$ and avoiding it, with cycle weight $2x^{\|\lambda\|}$. Let $Z_{\rm out}(\lambda)$ count disjoint cycles in $D$ surrounding and disjoint from $\lambda$ with the same weights. At a vertex of $\lambda$, call the corner convex or reflex when its interior angle is $2\pi/3$ or $4\pi/3$, respectively, and put $$c_\lambda= \begin{cases} \sqrt2,&v\text{ is a convex corner of }\lambda,\\ 2+\sqrt2,&v\text{ is a reflex corner of }\lambda. \end{cases}$$ Then $$\label{j:visit-identity} S_D(v)=3Z_v+\sum_{\lambda\ni v}c_\lambda x^{\|\lambda\|}Z_{\rm out}(\lambda).$$* *For each of the three incident face centers $f$, let $Z_D(f)$ be the partition of disjoint cycles in $D$ surrounding $f$, again with weight $2x^{\|\lambda\|}$. Put $k_\lambda=1$ at a convex corner and $k_\lambda=2$ at a reflex corner. Then $$\label{j:incident-face-partition} \sum_{f\sim v}Z_D(f) =3Z_v+\sum_{\lambda\ni v}2k_\lambda x^{\|\lambda\|} Z_{\rm out}(\lambda).$$ In particular the ordinary visit mass $\sum_{\gamma\ni v}x^{N(\gamma)}$ is comparable, with absolute positive constants, to $\sum_{f\sim v}Z_D(f)$.
  - Explanation: Expresses the signed visit mass through an interior vertex in terms of surrounding cycles and compares its ordinary mass to the nesting partitions at incident faces.
- **claim-separating-cycle-escape-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-localization-escape)): Fix $C>1$. For a contractible separating cycle, measure horizontal coordinates relative to the enclosed mark in its chosen disk lift. Let $\mathcal E_M$ consist of all noncontractible separating cycles and all contractible separating cycles whose chosen disk either reaches $\|x_{\rm horiz}\|\ge M/4$ or has diameter greater than $CM$. Then $$\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal E_M}w_\lambda \le (5\sqrt2+2)\sqrt{I_M}.$$ Every cycle outside $\mathcal E_M$ has a disk lift contained in the closed Euclidean ball of radius $CM$ about its enclosed mark.
  - Explanation: Controls the mass of noncontractible or poorly localized separating cycles by the incompatible-pair mass and confines the remaining disk lifts.
- **claim-physical-marked-bond-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-marked-physical)): Let the permitted cut have even $M$, and let both marked sites be horizontal. The positive sum $H^{\rm poly}$ is finite. The generic matrix element $H^{\rm flip}$ has a regular limit at the associated physical site list, and at that list $$H^{\rm flip}=H^{\rm poly}.$$ This holds for every order and every number of the two site types in the two nonempty lists; the unmarked lists may be empty.
  - Explanation: Proves finiteness of the positive marked-polygon mass and identifies it with the regular physical limit of the algebraic flip observable.
- **claim-unequal-marked-interval-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-unequal)): Use the physical tilted cylinder and horizontal-type marked bonds just defined. Its two cut intervals have $m+1$ and $n+1$ sites, with $n\ge m$ and $M=m+n+2$ even. In each unmarked list the logarithmic site coordinates have imaginary parts $-f$ and $1-f$, where $0\le f\le0.6$. Their respective counts differ from $m(1-f),mf$ in the first unmarked list and from $n(1-f),nf$ in the second by at most a fixed constant. Let $H^{\rm poly}$ be the sum of $x^{\|\lambda\|}$ over single unoriented polygons through the two specified bonds. Uniformly over these lists and their orders, for every $\epsilon>0$ there are $C_\epsilon$ and $m_\epsilon$ such that $$H^{\rm poly}\le C_\epsilon n^\epsilon m^{-4/3}(n/m)^{1/3} \qquad(n\ge m\ge m_\epsilon).$$ Both $C_\epsilon$ and $m_\epsilon$ may depend on the fixed bound for the count discrepancies.
  - Explanation: Bounds marked-polygon mass uniformly over site orders when both unmarked lists have the prescribed controlled proportions and the smaller interval is sufficiently large.
- **claim-generic-long-flip-spin-formula** (construction, [source](#stmt-j-marked-flip-formula)): For generic nonzero $X$ on consecutive nonempty lists $A,B$, $$\label{c7:eq-L} \begin{aligned} N(X)^2 H^{\rm flip}(X) &=cUV\sum_s q^{-6Q}C_s \prod_{a\in A'\cup B'}F_{s_a}(U,x_a)F_{s_a}(V,x_a),\\ (F_+,F_0,F_-)&=(e_5e_6,e_3e_5,e_2e_3),\qquad c=2-\sqrt2. \end{aligned}$$ The two endpoint variables $U,V$ are independent in this identity.
  - Explanation: Gives the generic marked flip as a finite spin sum with independent endpoint variables and explicit endpoint-to-site factors.
- **claim-shifted-orbital-nonvanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-shifted-nonvanishing)): Let $M=2L\ge2$, $w_j=i h_j$ with $h_j\in\mathbb R$ of spread at most one, and $x_j=e^{\eta w_j}$, where $\eta=\pi/4$. Define $$\mathcal S(X)=\mathcal P(X)\prod_{j<l}C(w_j-w_l), \qquad C(r)=\tanh(\pi r/6),$$ using the confluent value for equal sites. Then $\mathcal S(X)\ne0$ and $$\label{j:shifted-orbital-ratio} \frac{N(X)}{\mathcal S(X)} =\left(\frac23\right)^L \mathbb E_h\exp\!\left(\sum_{a=1}^L\phi(k_a)\right)>0, \qquad \phi(k)=\log\left(1+\frac{e^{-2k}}{1+e^{-4k}}\right).$$ Here $\mathbb E_h$ has ordered density on $0<k_1<\cdots<k_L$ proportional to $$\Delta(k^2)^2\prod_{a=1}^L\frac{k_a}{\sinh3k_a}\ I_h(k), \qquad I_h(k)=\int_{U(2L)} e^{\operatorname{tr}(D_k\mathcal U D_h\mathcal U^*)}\,d\mathcal U,$$ where $D_k=\operatorname{diag}(k_1,\ldots,k_L,-k_1,\ldots,-k_L)$ and $D_h=\operatorname{diag}(h_1-h_*,\ldots,h_M-h_*)$ for $h_*=(\max h_j+\min h_j)/2$. The measure on $U(2L)$ is normalized Haar measure. In particular $N(X)\ne0$. The nonvanishing also holds after multiplying every $x_j$ by the same nonzero scalar.
  - Explanation: Represents the shifted scalar ratio by a positive orbital expectation and proves nonvanishing throughout the stated spread range, including confluence and common rescaling.
- **claim-period-excluding-walk-summability** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-period-excluded)): Fix a nonzero lattice translation $P$ and a honeycomb vertex $v$. The total critical weight of plane SAWs starting at $v$ whose visited vertices are distinct modulo $P$ is finite. The empty walk may be included. The bound may depend on $P$.
  - Explanation: Proves finite critical mass of plane walks that never repeat a vertex modulo a fixed nonzero period; the bound is allowed to depend on that period.
- **claim-arc-turn-and-seam-phase** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-marked-phase)): Let $T(X)$ be the total turn of the lifted arc, and let $K$ be its integer signed number of eastward crossings of the upper seam rays $\{\ell M\}\times(0,\infty)$, summed over $\ell$. Then $$\label{j:marked-phase-identities} T(X)=-2\pi\bigl(C_{\rm per}(i)+C_{\rm per}(j)+2C_0\bigr), \qquad K=C_0+\frac{k}{2}.$$ Consequently, for $q=e^{i\pi/4}$, $$q^{4C_0}i^k(-1)^K=e^{2\pi iK}=1.$$
  - Explanation: Relates arc turning to periodic cut flux and seam crossings, producing the exact phase cancellation needed for the physical marked identity.
- **claim-fixed-list-marked-regulator** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-marked-regulated-limit)): For every $T>8r$ and fixed finite initial lists and endpoint coordinate as above, the Wick expansion in species $\sigma$ terminates after order $n_\sigma$ and extends to coalescing own lists in the same neighborhood. As $T\to\infty$ with generic initial data fixed, $$\label{j:marked-regulator-limit} \mathfrak C_T^L\longrightarrow \frac{N(X)^2H^{\rm flip}(X)} {cU^2P_0(W_1,W_2)\prod_{a\in A'\cup B'}F_0(U,x_a)^2}.$$ This statement is initially at values where the displayed denominator is nonzero.
  - Explanation: Proves termination and own-list confluence for the marked regulator and identifies its fixed-list infinite-period limit where its normalization is nonzero.
- **claim-exact-marked-horizontal-gas** (theorem, [source](#stmt-j-marked-gas-identity)): Fix a sufficiently small negative pre-collision displacement $d_-$ in the stability range, with $\|d_-\|<1/8$, and use post-collision displacement $d=1/8$. For all sufficiently large integer periods $T$, chosen independently of the finite site counts, and for every pair of finite initial real lists and real endpoint coordinate in the fixed neighborhood above, the gas $Z_T^L$ converges absolutely and $$\label{c7:eq-M} \begin{aligned} \mathfrak C_T^L &=c(T)Z_T^L \exp\left(\frac12\int_T A^tD(I+gE)A -i\int_T A^tD\mathbf1\,d_T+R_T^d\right),\\ R_T^d&=-\frac{\|\mathbf1\|^2}{4\pi} \int_T d_T(l-L_*)d_T,\qquad \mathbf1=(1,1)^t. \end{aligned}$$ Here $c(T)$ is exactly the scalar in <a href="#c7:regulator-gas" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="c7:regulator-gas">[c7:regulator-gas]</a>. The identity includes coalescing own lists by continuity. The absolute convergence bounds may depend on the fixed lists, $T$, and the fixed displacements. The same identity holds along $T=bn$ for a sufficiently large fixed integer block length $b$ and positive integers $n$. No estimate uniform as a displacement tends to zero is asserted.
  - Explanation: Identifies the marked regulator with a convergent varying-angle gas and explicit scalar contractions at fixed finite lists on a common supported period domain.
- **claim-uniform-shifted-normalizer-growth** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-shifted-normalizer-bound)): For every $\varepsilon>0$, for all sufficiently large even $M$, uniformly over real $h_j$ of spread at most one, $$\label{c7:eq-P} \frac{N(X)}{\mathcal S(X)} \ge \left(\frac23\right)^{M/2}M^{5/48-\varepsilon}, \qquad x_j=e^{i\eta h_j}.$$
  - Explanation: Supplies a uniform lower bound on the shifted scalar ratio with arbitrary exponent slack over even site counts and heights of bounded spread.
- **claim-stability-at-eighth-displacement** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-stability-eighth)): For the post-collision gas at $d=1/8$, the conclusion of Theorem <a href="#j:absolute-stability" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="j:absolute-stability">15</a> holds, with constants uniform in $T$ and in $\theta$ in a fixed compact subset of $\mathbb C$.
  - Explanation: Extends the required post-collision stability conclusion to the specified marked-gas displacement with uniform period and compact-angle control.
- **claim-uniform-shifted-site-suppression** (bound, [source](#stmt-j-shifted-suppression)): There are constants $0<\delta_0<1/16$ and $c_1>0$ with the following property. For every fixed discrepancy bound $0\le C_0<\infty$ there is $n_0(C_0)$ such that, for integers $n\ge n_0(C_0)$, the conclusion below holds uniformly in $f\in[0,3/5]$.* *Partition a list of $n$ real heights into groups $I_0,I_1$ such that $$\bigl\|\|I_0\|-n(1-f)\bigr\|\le C_0,\qquad \bigl\|\|I_1\|-nf\bigr\|\le C_0.$$ Suppose $$\|h_a+f\|<\delta_0\quad(a\in I_0),\qquad \|h_a-(1-f)\|<\delta_0\quad(a\in I_1).$$ For every real $x$ and every $\tau\in\{P,O_+,O_-,U,L\}$, $$\label{j:shifted-suppression-bound} \left\|\prod_{a=1}^n\omega_\tau(x;h_a)\right\| \le \exp\!\left(-c_1 n e^{-\kappa_1\|x\|}\right), \qquad \kappa_1=\pi/3.$$ The sums of the one-site logarithms chosen to vanish at either infinity are $O(n e^{-\kappa_1\|x\|})$ there, uniformly in these lists. The proposition applies separately to each species.
  - Explanation: Shows that complete site products suppress each specified particle type uniformly near the physical heights when the proportion discrepancies remain bounded.
- **claim-mixed-propagation-radius** (bound, [source](#stmt-c7-mixed-radius)): For every real $\theta$, $$\label{c7:eq-X} r(X_\theta)\le r_X^+, \qquad r_X^+=\exp\!\left[b\left(-\frac{5\pi}{96} +\frac1{6\sqrt3}\right)\right].$$
  - Explanation: Bounds the mixed operator radius by comparing equivalent regulators through the coupled and marginal gas descriptions at fixed period before the auxiliary site-count limit.
- **claim-two-exterior-gap-coefficients** (theorem, [source](#stmt-c7-two-gap)): Let $E_+,E_-$ be Hilbert–Schmidt operators on a complex Hilbert space, each with spectral radius one. Write $\mathcal P_\pm=\{\zeta\in\sigma(E_\pm):\|\zeta\|=1\}$ for their finite nonempty peripheral spectra. For $\zeta\in\mathcal P_\pm$, let $P_\zeta^\pm$ be the Riesz projection, $J_\zeta^\pm=(E_\pm-\zeta I)P_\zeta^\pm$, and choose $q_\zeta^\pm\ge1$ to be its nilpotent order on $\operatorname{ran}P_\zeta^\pm$. Let $C$ be trace class. For $i=1,2,3,4$, let $\mathscr W_i$ be a countable family of bounded operators with integer lengths $\ell(W)\ge0$ such that, for fixed $\varepsilon,B>0$, $$\sum_{W\in\mathscr W_i}e^{\varepsilon\ell(W)}\\|W\\|\le B.$$ Fix an integer $L\ge0$. For integers $N\ge1$ with $g=2N-L\ge0$, put $$\begin{gathered} F_{N,L}=\sum_{\substack{W_i\in\mathscr W_i\\ \ell_+\le g,\ \ell_-\le g}} \operatorname{tr}\bigl(CW_1E_+^{g-\ell_+}W_2W_3 E_-^{g-\ell_-}W_4\bigr),\\ \ell_+=\ell(W_1)+\ell(W_2),\quad \ell_-=\ell(W_3)+\ell(W_4). \end{gathered}$$ Suppose $F_{N,L}-R\operatorname{tr}E_+^{4N}\to0$ for a scalar $R$ as $N\to\infty$ at this fixed $L$. For either sign define $$\mathcal B_\zeta^\pm(z,\ell)= \sum_{a=0}^{q_\zeta^\pm-1} \binom{z-\ell}{a}\zeta^{-a}(J_\zeta^\pm)^aP_\zeta^\pm.$$ The following series is coefficientwise absolutely convergent and defines a polynomial: $$\begin{aligned} \mathscr P_{\zeta,\eta}(z)={}& \sum_{W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4}\zeta^{-\ell_+}\eta^{-\ell_-}\\ &\quad\cdot\operatorname{tr}\bigl(CW_1\mathcal B_\zeta^+(z,\ell_+)W_2W_3 \mathcal B_\eta^-(z,\ell_-)W_4\bigr). \end{aligned}$$ Then for every frequency $\beta$ in $\{\alpha^4:\alpha\in\mathcal P_+\}\cup \{(\zeta\eta)^2:\zeta\in\mathcal P_+,\eta\in\mathcal P_-\}$, $$\label{c7:two-gap-frequency} \begin{aligned} R\sum_{\substack{\alpha\in\mathcal P_+\\\alpha^4=\beta}} \operatorname{rank}P_\alpha^+ &=\sum_{\substack{\zeta\in\mathcal P_+,\eta\in\mathcal P_-\\ (\zeta\eta)^2=\beta}} (\zeta\eta)^{-L}\mathscr P_{\zeta,\eta}(-L). \end{aligned}$$ In particular $$\|R\|\le K(1+L)^h\\|C\\|_1, \qquad h=\max_{\zeta,\eta}(q_\zeta^++q_\eta^--2),$$ where $K$ depends only on $E_\pm$, $\varepsilon$, and $B$, and is independent of $C,L,R$.
  - Explanation: Groups colliding peripheral frequencies for traces with exterior portions on both sides and bounds the extracted scalar using the central trace norm and a polynomial offset cost.
- **claim-few-good-vertices-summability** (bound, [source](#stmt-c7-bad-windows)): For a sufficiently large fixed $K$, $$\sum_{\lambda:\,\#\{\text{good vertices of }\lambda\}<\|\lambda\|/2} x^{\|\lambda\|}\|\lambda\|^2<\infty,$$ where polygons are counted modulo translations.
  - Explanation: Shows that polygons with too few windows using every bond orientation have finite length-square weighted mass modulo translations.
- **claim-selected-bond-pair-cylinder-construction** (construction, [source](#stmt-c7-selected-pair)): Let $\lambda$ be a planar polygon of diameter at most $H$, and let $v_1,v_2$ be good vertices. Put $r_K=(K-1/2)/\sqrt3$. If $\|v_2-v_1\|>4\sqrt{19}\,r_K$, one can assign used bonds $e_1,e_2$ within their respective windows so that the following holds after a lattice rotation or reflection. Both bonds cross horizontal tessellation sides, and their midpoint displacement is $$\delta=a+b\tau,\qquad a\ge1,\quad b\ge0,\quad f=\frac{b}{a+b}<0.6.$$ There is a permitted cut with these two horizontal marked sites and, after a common rescaling, physical logarithmic heights $-f,1-f$. Its interval sizes are $m+1,n+1$, its period has an even number $M=m+n+2$ of sites, and its unmarked count discrepancies from the proportions $1-f,f$ are at most $f$. It has $n\ge m$, $m\asymp\|\delta\|$, and $n\asymp H$ above a fixed distance cutoff. Projection to this cylinder is injective on the polygons of diameter at most $H$ containing the fixed ordered bond pair, when their first bond is fixed in the plane.
  - Explanation: Assigns nearby used bonds to sufficiently separated good vertices and constructs a permitted cylinder meeting the marked estimate's parity, proportions, size, and injection requirements.

        "exact_quote": "For every list size $M$, the functions $N_l$ are symmetric homogeneous polynomials of individual degree at most $l(M-1)$ for $M\\ge1$, and $$\\mathcal J=N N_2^*.$$ For $l=1,2$ and $X=(u,Z)$ of size $M\\ge1$, their deletion values are $$\\label{j:normalizer-deletion}\nN_l(0,Z)=\\left(\\prod_{z\\in Z}z^l\\right)N_l(Z),\n\\qquad [u^{l(M-1)}]N_l(u,Z)=N_l(Z).$$ For $\\delta=2,3$ all three satisfy $$\\label{j:normalizer-fusion}\nN_l(u,q^\\delta u,Z)=N_l(u,q^\\delta u)\\ \\prod_{z\\in Z}\\ell_\\delta(u,z)^l\\ N_l(X_{\\rm red}),\\qquad\n X_{\\rm red}=\\begin{cases}(qu,Z)&\\delta=2,\\\\Z&\\delta=3.\\end{cases}$$ At two sites, $$N(u,v)=u+v,\\qquad\nN_2^*(u,v)=u^2+2(1+\\sqrt2)uv+v^2.$$ Finally, $N$ and $N_2^*$ are nonzero at every homogeneous list $(b,\\ldots,b)$ with $b\\ne0$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-j-selected-vacuum-vectors",
        "exact_quote": "Let $M\\ge1$, let $X=(x_1,\\ldots,x_M)$ be generic and nonzero, and choose $t_j$ with $t_j^2=x_j$. For $\\sigma\\in\\{-1,0,1\\}^M$ with $\\sum_j\\sigma_j=0$, define from the vacuum-normalized vectors $R_i=\\Pi_i|0\\rangle$ and $L_{-i}=\\langle0|\\Pi_{-i}$ the functions $$V_\\sigma^R(X)=\n\\frac{N(X)(R_i)_\\sigma}{\\prod_jt_j^{\\sigma_j^2}},\n\\qquad\nV_\\sigma^L(X)=\n\\frac{N(X)(L_{-i})_\\sigma}{\\prod_jt_j^{\\sigma_j^2}}.$$ They are independent of the choices of square-root signs and extend to polynomials in $\\mathbb C[x_1,\\ldots,x_M]$ satisfying $$\\deg_{x_j}V_\\sigma^\\epsilon\\le M-1-\\sigma_j^2\n\\qquad(\\epsilon=R,L).$$ Write $X_{\\widehat j}$ and $\\widehat\\sigma$ for deletion of coordinate $j$, and set $V_\\varnothing^R=V_\\varnothing^L=1$.         "exact_quote": "For two consecutive lists $A,B$, allowing either to be empty, and $h\\ne0$, put $\\mathscr G(X;A,B)=L_-D_A R_+$. Then $$\\begin{split}\nN(X)^2\\mathscr G(X;A,B)\n =\\sum_{\\substack{\\sigma\\in\\{-1,0,1\\}^M\\\\ \\sum_j\\sigma_j=0}}\n (ih)^{\\sum_{j\\in A}\\sigma_j}\n \\left(\\prod_jx_j^{\\sigma_j^2}\\right)\n V_\\sigma^L(X)V_\\sigma^R(X).\n\\end{split}$$ The empty-list value is 1. For $M\\ge1$ it is a polynomial in $X$ with Laurent polynomial coefficients in $h$, of individual degree at most $2(M-1)$. For a deleted site $j$, its value at $x_j=0$ is the reduced polynomial times $\\prod_{k\\ne j}x_k^2$, and its coefficient of $x_j^{2(M-1)}$ is the reduced polynomial.         "exact_quote": "The family $\\mathscr F_{A,B}$ is the unique family in $\\mathbb C(h)[X]$ with the following properties. The empty-list value is 1.         "anchor": "stmt-c7-regulated-pfaffian",
        "exact_quote": "For every fixed $T>0$, $m\\in\\mathbb N_0$, and $\\theta\\in\\mathbb C$, on the full-probability event of analytic samples described above, the Wick expansion in <a href=\"#c7:contour-current\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"c7:contour-current\">[c7:contour-current]</a> terminates after order $m$ in each species. The average <a href=\"#c7:regulated-contour\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"c7:regulated-contour\">[c7:regulated-contour]</a> is holomorphic there and its denominator is nonzero.         "anchor": "stmt-c7-angular-trace",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $T>0$, $m\\in\\mathbb N_0$, $\\theta\\in\\mathbb C$, and a homogeneous analytic sample as above. The normalizing trace is $$Z_\\Gamma:=\\operatorname{Tr}\\Gamma\n=\\prod_{r\\in\\frac12+\\mathbb N_0}(1-\\mathbf q^{6r})>0.$$ For $s\\ge1$, if the folded coordinates have strictly increasing imaginary parts with total range less than $1$, then $$\\label{c7:angular-wick}\n\\left(-\\frac{2\\pi i}{a_*T}\\right)^s\n\\frac{\\operatorname{Tr}\\bigl(\\Gamma\\Psi_{j_1}(v_1)\\cdots\n \\Psi_{j_{2s}}(v_{2s})\\bigr)}{Z_\\Gamma}\n=\n\\operatorname{Pf}_{1\\le a,b\\le2s}\n C^{[T]}\\bigl(v_b-v_a+i(j_b-j_a)\\bigr).$$ The trace in this display denotes its absolutely convergent ordered mode sum. For $s=0$ both sides are $1$. The formula at other nonsingular coordinates is its meromorphic continuation; odd products vanish.*\n\n\n*Let $P_N$ project onto the energy-$N$ subspace, for $N\\in\\frac12\\mathbb N_0$. For a fixed finite word $Y$ of exponentials of the currents $X_{bc}(f)$, with periodic coefficients analytic on a common strip of positive width, there are $C,c>0$ such that $$\\label{c7:graded-current-bound}\n\\|P_{N'}YP_N\\|\\le C e^{C\\sqrt{N+1}}e^{-c|N'-N|}.$$ The constants can be taken locally uniform in numerical parameters multiplying the currents in the exponentials. In particular the energy-level trace with $\\Gamma$ is absolutely convergent, as are its exponential series of scalar trace coefficients.*\n\n\n*For the homogeneous contour expression <a href=\"#c7:contour-current\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"c7:contour-current\">[c7:contour-current]</a> and the fixed analytic sample, $$\\label{c7:four-current-trace}\n\\mathcal C_\\sigma\n=\\frac1{Z_\\Gamma}\\operatorname{Tr}_{\\rm gr}\\!\\left(\n \\Gamma e^{X_{23}(b_+^{-1})}e^{X_{21}(b)}\n e^{-X_{12}(b^{-1})}e^{-X_{16}(b_-)}\\right).$$ Here the absolutely convergent trace furnished by <a href=\"#c7:graded-current-bound\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"c7:graded-current-bound\">[c7:graded-current-bound]</a> is $$\\operatorname{Tr}_{\\rm gr}(\\Gamma Y)\n=\\sum_N\\mathbf q^N\n \\operatorname{tr}_{P_N\\mathcal F}(\\mathcal U P_NYP_N),$$ where $\\mathcal F$ is the fermionic exterior space. The convergence assertions concern this fixed sample.",
        "source_id": "PM-237.5"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-c7-gas-identity",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $d_-<0<d$ in the respective nonzero displacement ranges of Theorem <a href=\"#j:absolute-stability\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"j:absolute-stability\">15</a>, with $0<|d_-|<d<1/2$. Fix also a compact set $\\Omega\\subset\\mathbb C$ of values of $\\theta$. There is an integer $T_0$, independent of $m$, such that for every integer $T\\ge T_0$ and every finite integer $m\\ge0$, the gas <a href=\"#c7:gas-definition\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"c7:gas-definition\">[c7:gas-definition]</a> converges absolutely, uniformly for $\\theta\\in\\Omega$ at that $m,T$, and satisfies $$\\label{c7:regulator-gas}\n\\mathfrak C_{m,T}=c(T)e^{m^2\\kappa_T}Z_{m,T},\\qquad\nc(T)=\\frac{\\sqrt{8/9}}{8\\sqrt{2T}\\,D_\\ell}\n \\left(\\frac{\\sqrt T D_W}{Z_\\Gamma}\\right)^2D_g,\n\\qquad D_\\ell=\\sum_{j\\in8\\mathbb Z}e^{-4\\pi j^2/T}.$$ In particular it holds along $T=bn$ for any fixed integer block length $b\\ge T_0$ and every positive integer $n$. This common period domain allows $T$ to remain fixed while $m$ varies through finite integers. The absolute bounds may depend on $m,T$ and the fixed displacements; no bound uniform in $m$ or limiting assertion as $d_-\\uparrow0$ or $d\\downarrow0$ is made.",

        "exact_quote": "There is $0<d_0<1/2$ with the following property. Fix a compact set $\\Theta\\subset\\mathbb C$, and fix either a pre-collision displacement $-d_0<d<0$ or a post-collision displacement $0<d<d_0$. Give it a state path $p$ with jumps $-q_i$ and closure in $\\mathbb Z^2/8\\mathbb Z(1,-1)$. Let $n_j$ be the number of physical particles in $[j,j+1)$, and let $$p_{c,j}=\\frac{p_1(j+)+p_2(j+)}{\\sqrt2},\n\\qquad 0\\le j<T.$$ Then $$\\left|W_{d,\\theta}(\\mathcal Y,p)\\right|\n\\ \\le\\\n\\exp\\!\\left(CT-c\\sum_{j=0}^{T-1}(n_j^2+p_{c,j}^2)\\right)$$ in the post-collision case.       "exact_statement": "There is $0<d_0<1/2$ with the following property. Give it a state path $p$ with jumps $-q_i$ and closure in $\\mathbb Z^2/8\\mathbb Z(1,-1)$. Let $n_j$ be the number of physical particles in $[j,j+1)$, and let $$p_{c,j}=\\frac{p_1(j+)+p_2(j+)}{\\sqrt2},\n\\qquad 0\\le j<T.$$ Then $$\\left|W_{d,\\theta}(\\mathcal Y,p)\\right|\n\\ \\le\\\n\\exp\\!\\left(CT-c\\sum_{j=0}^{T-1}(n_j^2+p_{c,j}^2)\\right)$$ in the post-collision case.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-j-block-kernel",
        "exact_quote": "Use the state space, measure, and successor rule <a href=\"#j:successor-state\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:successor-state\">[j:successor-state]</a>. Suppose the local kernel satisfies <a href=\"#j:local-gauge\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:local-gauge\">[j:local-gauge]</a>, and use the tail data and edge operator <a href=\"#j:tail-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:tail-data\">[j:tail-data]</a>–<a href=\"#j:bargmann-edge\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:bargmann-edge\">[j:bargmann-edge]</a> with the bounds just proved. On $L^2$ of states with these Bargmann fibers, give an allowed edge the operator-valued kernel $$\\label{j:gauged-kernel}\n e^{\\Phi(S')-\\Phi(S)}w_\\theta(S,S')\\,\\mu(Y)\\,\\mathcal K(S,S'),$$ and give every other edge value zero. The choices of $\\mu(Y)$ used in this section are one, the indicator that every label is $M$ or $F_{\\rm pair}$, and the products of the specified balanced periodized or infinite-volume $B$ factors. Their per-particle factors have modulus at most one. For sufficiently large fixed $b$, these kernels are Hilbert–Schmidt uniformly in those choices and in $\\theta\\in D$. The same conclusion permits fixed polynomial factors in the particle counts. For the fixed gauge on $D$, the kernels form holomorphic families in Hilbert–Schmidt norm on the open parameter neighborhood $\\mathcal U_\\theta$, with bounds uniform on compact subsets.*\n\n\n*For a product of $n\\ge2$ such kernels, its trace is the absolutely convergent integral over closed successor sequences, with the gauge factors canceled and the Bargmann trace given by <a href=\"#j:bargmann-cycle\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:bargmann-cycle\">[j:bargmann-cycle]</a>. In particular, let $T_j$ carry the specified periodized $B_T$ site factors for block $j$. Then, in increasing block order, $$\\label{j:operator-gas-trace}\n \\operatorname{tr}\\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}T_j\n =\\det(I-A_0^n)^{-1}Z_{m,bn}.$$",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-j-trace-extraction",
        "exact_quote": "Let $E$ be a Hilbert–Schmidt operator on a complex Hilbert space with spectral radius one. Let $\\mathcal P=\\{\\zeta\\in\\sigma(E):|\\zeta|=1\\}$. For each $\\zeta\\in\\mathcal P$ let $P_\\zeta$ be its Riesz projection, $d_\\zeta=\\operatorname{rank}P_\\zeta$, and $J_\\zeta=(E-\\zeta I)P_\\zeta$, with $J_\\zeta^{q_\\zeta}=0$ on $\\operatorname{ran}P_\\zeta$. Let $C$ be trace class. Suppose two countable families of bounded operators $W_+,W_-$ have integer lengths $\\ell(W_\\pm)\\ge0$ and, for some $\\epsilon>0$, $$\\label{j:word-moment}\n \\sum_{W_\\pm}e^{\\epsilon\\ell(W_\\pm)}\\|W_\\pm\\|<\\infty.$$ For integers $s\\ge0$ put $$F_s=\\sum_{\\ell(W_+)+\\ell(W_-)\\le s}\n \\operatorname{tr}(CW_+E^{s-\\ell(W_+)-\\ell(W_-)}W_-).$$ Assume that $a\\ge0$ is an integer and $R\\in\\mathbb C$ satisfy $F_s-R\\operatorname{tr}E^{s+a}\\to0$ as $s\\to\\infty$. Only sufficiently large $s$, with $s+a\\ge2$, are used in this limit. Then the coefficientwise absolutely convergent polynomial $$\\mathcal P_\\zeta(z)=\\sum_{W_+,W_-}\\zeta^{-\\ell}\n \\operatorname{tr}\\left(CW_+\n \\left[\\sum_{t=0}^{q_\\zeta-1}\n \\binom{z-\\ell}{t}\\zeta^{-t}J_\\zeta^tP_\\zeta\\right]W_-\\right),\n \\quad \\ell=\\ell(W_+)+\\ell(W_-),$$ is identically $R d_\\zeta\\zeta^a$. In particular, $$R=\\frac{\\mathcal P_\\zeta(0)}{d_\\zeta\\zeta^a},\\qquad\n |R|\\le K\\|C\\|_1,$$ where $K$ depends on $E$ and the bounds in <a href=\"#j:word-moment\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:word-moment\">[j:word-moment]</a>, but not on $C$ or $a$. More precisely it may be chosen in terms of $\\epsilon$, the two weighted word sums, the finite nilpotent orders $q_\\zeta$, and the norms $\\|J_\\zeta^tP_\\zeta\\|$. Thus the conclusion is uniform for a family with uniform bounds on these data. No peripheral semisimplicity is assumed.",
        "source_id": "PM-237.5"
      },

        "exact_quote": "Fix $C>1$. For a contractible separating cycle, measure horizontal coordinates relative to the enclosed mark in its chosen disk lift.       },
      "evidence": [

        "anchor": "stmt-j-marked-gas-identity",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a sufficiently small negative pre-collision displacement $d_-$ in the stability range, with $|d_-|<1/8$, and use post-collision displacement $d=1/8$. For all sufficiently large integer periods $T$, chosen independently of the finite site counts, and for every pair of finite initial real lists and real endpoint coordinate in the fixed neighborhood above, the gas $Z_T^L$ converges absolutely and $$\\label{c7:eq-M}\n\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathfrak C_T^L\n &=c(T)Z_T^L\n \\exp\\left(\\frac12\\int_T A^tD(I+gE)A\n       -i\\int_T A^tD\\mathbf1\\,d_T+R_T^d\\right),\\\\\n R_T^d&=-\\frac{|\\mathbf1|^2}{4\\pi}\n              \\int_T d_T(l-L_*)d_T,\\qquad \\mathbf1=(1,1)^t.\n\\end{aligned}$$ Here $c(T)$ is exactly the scalar in <a href=\"#c7:regulator-gas\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"c7:regulator-gas\">[c7:regulator-gas]</a>. The identity includes coalescing own lists by continuity. The absolute convergence bounds may depend on the fixed lists, $T$, and the fixed displacements. The same identity holds along $T=bn$ for a sufficiently large fixed integer block length $b$ and positive integers $n$. No estimate uniform as a displacement tends to zero is asserted.",
        "source_id": "PM-237.5"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-j-marked-gas-identity",
          "exact_quote": "Fix a sufficiently small negative pre-collision displacement $d_-$ in the stability range, with $|d_-|<1/8$, and use post-collision displacement $d=1/8$.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-c7-two-gap",
        "exact_quote": "Let $E_+,E_-$ be Hilbert–Schmidt operators on a complex Hilbert space, each with spectral radius one. Write $\\mathcal P_\\pm=\\{\\zeta\\in\\sigma(E_\\pm):|\\zeta|=1\\}$ for their finite nonempty peripheral spectra. For $\\zeta\\in\\mathcal P_\\pm$, let $P_\\zeta^\\pm$ be the Riesz projection, $J_\\zeta^\\pm=(E_\\pm-\\zeta I)P_\\zeta^\\pm$, and choose $q_\\zeta^\\pm\\ge1$ to be its nilpotent order on $\\operatorname{ran}P_\\zeta^\\pm$. Let $C$ be trace class. For $i=1,2,3,4$, let $\\mathscr W_i$ be a countable family of bounded operators with integer lengths $\\ell(W)\\ge0$ such that, for fixed $\\varepsilon,B>0$, $$\\sum_{W\\in\\mathscr W_i}e^{\\varepsilon\\ell(W)}\\|W\\|\\le B.$$ Fix an integer $L\\ge0$. For integers $N\\ge1$ with $g=2N-L\\ge0$, put $$\\begin{gathered}\n F_{N,L}=\\sum_{\\substack{W_i\\in\\mathscr W_i\\\\\n                \\ell_+\\le g,\\ \\ell_-\\le g}}\n \\operatorname{tr}\\bigl(CW_1E_+^{g-\\ell_+}W_2W_3\n                           E_-^{g-\\ell_-}W_4\\bigr),\\\\\n \\ell_+=\\ell(W_1)+\\ell(W_2),\\quad\n       \\ell_-=\\ell(W_3)+\\ell(W_4).\n\\end{gathered}$$ Suppose $F_{N,L}-R\\operatorname{tr}E_+^{4N}\\to0$ for a scalar $R$ as $N\\to\\infty$ at this fixed $L$. For either sign define $$\\mathcal B_\\zeta^\\pm(z,\\ell)=\n \\sum_{a=0}^{q_\\zeta^\\pm-1}\n \\binom{z-\\ell}{a}\\zeta^{-a}(J_\\zeta^\\pm)^aP_\\zeta^\\pm.$$ The following series is coefficientwise absolutely convergent and defines a polynomial: $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathscr P_{\\zeta,\\eta}(z)={}&\n \\sum_{W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4}\\zeta^{-\\ell_+}\\eta^{-\\ell_-}\\\\\n &\\quad\\cdot\\operatorname{tr}\\bigl(CW_1\\mathcal B_\\zeta^+(z,\\ell_+)W_2W_3\n                              \\mathcal B_\\eta^-(z,\\ell_-)W_4\\bigr).\n\\end{aligned}$$ Then for every frequency $\\beta$ in $\\{\\alpha^4:\\alpha\\in\\mathcal P_+\\}\\cup\n \\{(\\zeta\\eta)^2:\\zeta\\in\\mathcal P_+,\\eta\\in\\mathcal P_-\\}$, $$\\label{c7:two-gap-frequency}\n\\begin{aligned}\n R\\sum_{\\substack{\\alpha\\in\\mathcal P_+\\\\\\alpha^4=\\beta}}\n       \\operatorname{rank}P_\\alpha^+\n &=\\sum_{\\substack{\\zeta\\in\\mathcal P_+,\\eta\\in\\mathcal P_-\\\\\n                   (\\zeta\\eta)^2=\\beta}}\n       (\\zeta\\eta)^{-L}\\mathscr P_{\\zeta,\\eta}(-L).\n\\end{aligned}$$ In particular $$|R|\\le K(1+L)^h\\|C\\|_1,\n \\qquad h=\\max_{\\zeta,\\eta}(q_\\zeta^++q_\\eta^--2),$$ where $K$ depends only on $E_\\pm$, $\\varepsilon$, and $B$, and is independent of $C,L,R$.",
        "source_id": "PM-237.5"
      },

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Honeycomb graph and Euclidean embedding** ([source](#pm-h-3)): Let $\mathbb H$ be the honeycomb graph formed by the centers of the triangles of a regular triangular tessellation of side length one.
- **Boundary port** ([source](#pm-h-3)): A port is the midpoint of a tessellation side on the boundary of a region.
- **Port-to-port first-exit walk** ([source](#pm-h-3)): A port-to-port walk traverses distinct triangle centers and stops at its first boundary exit.
- **Critical path activity** ([source](#pm-h-3)): If it visits $N$ centers, its critical weight is $x^N$, where $$x=(2+\sqrt2)^{-1/2}.$$
- **Polygon counting convention** ([source](#pm-h-3)): All polygon sums below count unoriented, unrooted cycles.
- **Translation-class polygon sum** ([source](#pm-h-3)): A sum modulo translations counts each lattice translation class once.
- **Cycle incompatibility** ([source](#pm-h-3)): Two cycles are incompatible if they share a vertex; a cycle is incompatible with itself.
- **Macroscopic ordered hexagon chords** ([source](#pm-h-3)): Let $\mathcal C_R$ consist of the ordered first-exit chords of $D_R$ whose diameter is at least $R/10$.
- **Exponent asymptotic notation** ([source](#pm-h-3)): For a positive quantity $F(R)$, the notation $F(R)=R^{a+o(1)}$ means $\log F(R)/\log R\to a$.
- **Scalar two-list vacuum observable** ([source](#stmt-j-scalar-vacuum-polynomial)): For two consecutive lists $A,B$, allowing either to be empty, and $h\ne0$, put $\mathscr G(X;A,B)=L_-D_A R_+$.
- **Block configuration** ([source](#j:successor-state)): A block configuration $Y$ is a finite ordered list of positions $t$ and particle labels.
- **Generic marked flip observable** ([source](#pm-h-65)): For a generic nonzero site list $X$ on the same two lists, define a separate algebraic quantity $$\label{j:marked-flip-definition} H^{\rm flip}(X)= L_- f_i\, i^{\sum_{a\in A'}s_a^{\rm phys}} e_j R_+,\qquad f_i=\|-\rangle_i\langle+\|,\quad e_j=\|+\rangle_j\langle-\|.$$
- **Good polygon vertex** ([source](#pm-h-91)): A vertex of a polygon is called good if the cyclic window of $2K$ path edges centered at that vertex uses bonds crossing tessellation sides of all three orientations.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-local-exchange-fusion** [claim](#stmt-j-local-exchange-fusion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-local-exchange-fusion): Check the local blocks at fusion parameters, prove inversion and intertwining, then determine the exchange identity by trigonometric interpolation. -> Meromorphic exchange, inversion, and fusion identities.
- **step-fusion-quotient** [claim](#stmt-j-local-restriction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-local-restriction): Transport the invariant action through the embedding and use the matching-site image inclusion to obtain quotient vanishing. -> Restricted transfer action and holomorphic quotient divisibility.
- **step-fourier-kernel** [claim](#stmt-j-fourier-kernel) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-fourier-kernel): Evaluate residues on rectangles, sum the geometric series, and extend by dominated convergence and analyticity. -> Scalar Fourier transform and local parameter differentiation.
- **step-scalar-normalizers** [claim](#stmt-j-scalar-normalizers) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-scalar-normalizers): Remove apparent poles by alternating divisibility, derive deletion and fusion evaluations, and prove homogeneous nonvanishing through positive Fourier Gram forms. -> Polynomial normalizers, factorization, and homogeneous nonvanishing.
- **step-separated-scales** [claim](#stmt-j-separated-scales) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-separated-scales): Use inactive-site charge changes to order the grading and collect the remaining phases into an effective twist and common similarity. -> Triangular scale blocks and their common diagonal conjugation.
- **step-selected-vacuum-polynomiality** [claim](#stmt-j-selected-vacuum-vectors) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-selected-vacuum-vectors): Analyze simple probe projections and pair crossings at generic divisors, separate the selected row and column poles, then control coordinate endpoints and apply unique factorization. -> Polynomial selected vacuum components with degree and deletion rules.
- **step-scalar-vacuum-polynomial** [claim](#stmt-j-scalar-vacuum-polynomial) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-scalar-vacuum-polynomial): Expand the diagonal insertion in the spin basis and apply component degree and deletion bounds. -> Cleared scalar polynomial and its endpoint reductions.
- **step-scalar-characterization** [claim](#stmt-j-scalar-characterization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-scalar-characterization): Use same-group exchange and fusion, inductive polynomial zero counting, and paired-scale normalization to remove the balanced residual coefficient. -> Unique characterization of the scalar polynomial family.
- **step-finite-spin-sum** [claim](#stmt-j-finite-spin-formula) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-finite-spin-formula): Verify cancellation of apparent poles and match deletion, fusion, degree, and paired-scale data against the unique characterization. -> Exact finite spin expression with polynomial confluence.
- **step-regulated-pfaffian** [claim](#stmt-c7-regulated-pfaffian) / [proof](#proof-stmt-c7-regulated-pfaffian): Use site residues and fermionic exclusion for termination, combine the neutral Gaussian quadratic before taking the period limit, and identify the limiting residue expression with the spin sum. -> Holomorphic finite regulator and fixed-site infinite-period limit.
- **step-conditional-angular-trace** [claim](#stmt-c7-angular-trace) / [proof](#proof-stmt-c7-angular-trace): Compute mode contractions by cyclicity, prove graded current bounds, and deform the finite contour coefficients to ordered current exponentials. -> Absolutely convergent conditional angular trace identities.
- **step-stability-coercivity** [claim](#stmt-j-stability-coercivity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-stability-coercivity): Split the signed-height matrix into even and odd sectors, prove core and displaced Schur positivity, and retain count and charge coercivity after removing the fixed nullspace. -> Coercive residual symbol and nonnegative physical high-frequency limit.
- **step-absolute-stability** [claim](#stmt-j-absolute-stability) / [proof](#pm-h-42): Drop nonnegative pair potentials, cancel the charge singularity against the state square, and use Gaussian smoothing to control box counts and charges. -> Quadratic absolute confinement and summability at fixed displacement.
- **step-exact-gas** [claim](#stmt-c7-gas-identity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-c7-gas-identity): Evaluate conditional currents in oscillator coordinates, integrate absolutely on pre-collision contours, add the collision residue, and complete the state action with its exact scalar normalization. -> Exact convergent horizontal gas on the supported integer periods.
- **step-block-kernel** [claim](#stmt-j-block-kernel) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-block-kernel): Construct a confining measurable gauge and an affine Bargmann tail propagator, then integrate the fiber trace over closed successor sequences. -> Hilbert–Schmidt gas kernels and exact closed-product traces.
- **step-signed-trace-extraction** [claim](#stmt-j-trace-extraction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-trace-extraction): Expand every peripheral Riesz block with its nilpotent powers, control word tails by exponential moments, and extract exponential-polynomial coefficients by Cesàro means. -> Scalar coefficient bound without division by a cancelling trace.
- **step-even-log-statistic** [claim](#stmt-j-even-log-statistic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-even-log-statistic): Analyze the even orthogonal-polynomial kernel and both of its peaks, establish a smaller commutator fluctuation, and integrate the tilted Gram determinant derivatives. -> Logarithmic determinant asymptotic for the homogeneous scalar normalization.
- **step-orbital-pinning** [claim](#stmt-j-orbital-pin) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-orbital-pin): Pin the determinant density at the origin, apply its adjugate formula, and compare the resulting determinant ratio through positive interlacing integrals. -> Positive expectation bounds for the boundary residue.
- **step-orbital-derivative** [claim](#stmt-j-orbital-ward) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-orbital-ward): Differentiate the unitary orbital integral using conjugation symmetry and sum the resulting squared matrix-entry identities. -> Uniform logarithmic derivative bounds.
- **step-gamma-comparison** [claim](#stmt-j-boundary-gamma-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-boundary-gamma-comparison): Compare logarithmic slopes of Gamma and orbital weights, use pure-law association, and condition on the controlled initial-point event. -> Stochastic comparisons for the pinned decreasing product.
- **step-boundary-arch-exponent** [claim](#stmt-j-boundary) / [proof](#j:wedge-comparison): Evaluate the boundary increment through pinned Gamma statistics, obtain balance saturation and the deficit tail, then compare reflected wedges to control the radius tail. -> Boundary arch radius exponent and endpoint-tail bound.
- **step-extremal-segment** [claim](#stmt-j-extremal-segment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-extremal-segment): Extend the extrema endpoints to adjacent port lines and apply the exhausted convex boundary balance with bounded extension multiplicity. -> Absolute endpoint-summed critical segment bound.
- **step-convex-cap** [claim](#stmt-j-convex-cap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-convex-cap): Subtract the signed balances of nested convex domains, cancel common chords, and compare their positive real coefficients. -> Comparison of lost chord mass and artificial exit mass.
- **step-interior-visit** [claim](#stmt-j-visit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-visit): Remove the triangle at the visit vertex, subtract path balances, and cancel first contacts against nested cycle backgrounds before comparing corner coefficients. -> Visit and incident-face identities with positive comparison constants.
- **step-cycle-localization** [claim](#stmt-j-localization-escape) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-localization-escape): Use reflected and translated wide disks, rotated nonwide disks, and vertical ordering of noncontractible cycles to force incompatible pairs. -> Escape mass bound and confinement of the remaining lifts.
- **step-cylinder-and-planar-exponents** [claim](#stmt-j-cylinder) / [proof](#c7:cylinder-exponent): Combine exact gas traces and signed coefficient extraction with homogeneous Pfaffian normalization, propagate the positive lower exponent analytically, then localize cycles to compare planar nesting partitions. -> Cylinder pressure, incompatible-pair bound, complex-angle bound, and planar nesting exponent.
- **step-generic-marked-flip** [claim](#stmt-j-marked-flip-formula) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-marked-flip-formula): Resolve partial monodromy spectra, determine forced amplitude factors from fusion and degree bounds, and fix the endpoint multiplier by separated pair scales. -> Generic long-flip formula with independent endpoints.
- **step-shifted-nonvanishing** [claim](#stmt-j-shifted-nonvanishing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-shifted-nonvanishing): Express the Pfaffian through paired exponential determinants and a positive unitary orbital integral, then pass to coinciding heights by domination. -> Exact positive scalar ratio and shifted normalizer nonvanishing.
- **step-period-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-j-period-excluded) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-period-excluded): Decompose slab crossings into irreducible blocks, exclude a positive-weight word repeating modulo the period, and sum decreasing extremal-span lists. -> Finite total critical mass for period-excluding walks.
- **step-marked-arc-phase** [claim](#stmt-j-marked-phase) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-marked-phase): Lift argument variations along embedded arcs and their translates, then compute upper-ray flux including endpoint half-atoms. -> Turn and seam identities giving exact phase cancellation.
- **step-physical-marked-identity** [claim](#stmt-j-marked-physical) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-marked-phase-2): Continue the selected vectors using shifted nonvanishing, identify physical vacuum limits through summable arc tails, and cancel the phases of the marked arcs. -> Finite positive marked-polygon mass equal to the algebraic physical limit.
- **step-fixed-list-marked-regulator** [claim](#stmt-j-marked-regulated-limit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-marked-regulated-limit): Use own-site residues for finite Wick termination and compute the changed source and endpoint contractions before the fixed-list period limit. -> Marked regulator confluence and normalized fixed-list limit.
- **step-eighth-displacement-stability** [claim](#stmt-j-stability-eighth) / [proof](#proof-stmt-j-stability-eighth): Derive exact even and odd Schur complements from the physical height lists and certify their signs through positive transformed polynomial coefficients and endpoint gaps. -> Absolute stability at the marked post-collision displacement.

          "anchor": "stmt-j-block-kernel",
          "exact_quote": "Use the state space, measure, and successor rule <a href=\"#j:successor-state\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:successor-state\">[j:successor-state]</a>. Suppose the local kernel satisfies <a href=\"#j:local-gauge\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:local-gauge\">[j:local-gauge]</a>, and use the tail data and edge operator <a href=\"#j:tail-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:tail-data\">[j:tail-data]</a>–<a href=\"#j:bargmann-edge\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:bargmann-edge\">[j:bargmann-edge]</a> with the bounds just proved. On $L^2$ of states with these Bargmann fibers, give an allowed edge the operator-valued kernel $$\\label{j:gauged-kernel}\n e^{\\Phi(S')-\\Phi(S)}w_\\theta(S,S')\\,\\mu(Y)\\,\\mathcal K(S,S'),$$ and give every other edge value zero. The choices of $\\mu(Y)$ used in this section are one, the indicator that every label is $M$ or $F_{\\rm pair}$, and the products of the specified balanced periodized or infinite-volume $B$ factors. Their per-particle factors have modulus at most one. For sufficiently large fixed $b$, these kernels are Hilbert–Schmidt uniformly in those choices and in $\\theta\\in D$. The same conclusion permits fixed polynomial factors in the particle counts. For the fixed gauge on $D$, the kernels form holomorphic families in Hilbert–Schmidt norm on the open parameter neighborhood $\\mathcal U_\\theta$, with bounds uniform on compact subsets.*\n\n\n*For a product of $n\\ge2$ such kernels, its trace is the absolutely convergent integral over closed successor sequences, with the gauge factors canceled and the Bargmann trace given by <a href=\"#j:bargmann-cycle\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:bargmann-cycle\">[j:bargmann-cycle]</a>.           "anchor": "stmt-j-trace-extraction",
          "exact_quote": "Let $E$ be a Hilbert–Schmidt operator on a complex Hilbert space with spectral radius one. Let $\\mathcal P=\\{\\zeta\\in\\sigma(E):|\\zeta|=1\\}$. For each $\\zeta\\in\\mathcal P$ let $P_\\zeta$ be its Riesz projection, $d_\\zeta=\\operatorname{rank}P_\\zeta$, and $J_\\zeta=(E-\\zeta I)P_\\zeta$, with $J_\\zeta^{q_\\zeta}=0$ on $\\operatorname{ran}P_\\zeta$. Let $C$ be trace class. Suppose two countable families of bounded operators $W_+,W_-$ have integer lengths $\\ell(W_\\pm)\\ge0$ and, for some $\\epsilon>0$, $$\\label{j:word-moment}\n \\sum_{W_\\pm}e^{\\epsilon\\ell(W_\\pm)}\\|W_\\pm\\|<\\infty.$$ For integers $s\\ge0$ put $$F_s=\\sum_{\\ell(W_+)+\\ell(W_-)\\le s}\n \\operatorname{tr}(CW_+E^{s-\\ell(W_+)-\\ell(W_-)}W_-).$$ Assume that $a\\ge0$ is an integer and $R\\in\\mathbb C$ satisfy $F_s-R\\operatorname{tr}E^{s+a}\\to0$ as $s\\to\\infty$. Only sufficiently large $s$, with $s+a\\ge2$, are used in this limit. Then the coefficientwise absolutely convergent polynomial $$\\mathcal P_\\zeta(z)=\\sum_{W_+,W_-}\\zeta^{-\\ell}\n \\operatorname{tr}\\left(CW_+\n \\left[\\sum_{t=0}^{q_\\zeta-1}\n \\binom{z-\\ell}{t}\\zeta^{-t}J_\\zeta^tP_\\zeta\\right]W_-\\right),\n \\quad \\ell=\\ell(W_+)+\\ell(W_-),$$ is identically $R d_\\zeta\\zeta^a$. In particular, $$R=\\frac{\\mathcal P_\\zeta(0)}{d_\\zeta\\zeta^a},\\qquad\n |R|\\le K\\|C\\|_1,$$ where $K$ depends on $E$ and the bounds in <a href=\"#j:word-moment\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"j:word-moment\">[j:word-moment]</a>, but not on $C$ or $a$. More precisely it may be chosen in terms of $\\epsilon$, the two weighted word sums, the finite nilpotent orders $q_\\zeta$, and the norms $\\|J_\\zeta^tP_\\zeta\\|$. Thus the conclusion is uniform for a family with uniform bounds on these data. No peripheral semisimplicity is assumed.",
